name: 2nd Apron Left Side
text: [overview] Start on angling cracks by the snow tongue, trend left under a little roof, then work through 500-600 ft of fractured rock at 5.6, some 5.7, to a grassy terrace.

name: Andrews Glacier
text: [overview] A well-known landmark that is possibly the sole non-technical glacier in the Park at certain times of year.
[overview] Late summer and fall turn it to alpine ice, so crampons are advisable, and once snow has fallen, avalanches can be a hazard.
[overview] In winter the surface may be soft snow or hard wind crust, at a steeper angle overall.
[overview] Later in the season, the left (south) edge may allow bypassing the snow, reportedly tricky depending on melt-out.
[detailed_rack] Pickets are a good choice if protection is needed.

name: Box of Candy Couloir
text: [approach] Begin at the Glacier Gorge trailhead and walk toward Andrews Glacier.
[approach] At Andrews Tarn, near the foot of the glacier, climb up the glacier while trending to the left.
[approach] The couloir hugs the rock wall on that side, and you are at its start when a snow, ice and rock ramp heads south.
[approach] Small crevasses near the bottom of the glacier can be deep, so take care around them.
[descent_text] Hike over to Andrews Glacier, descend it, and rejoin the main trail back to the trailhead.

name: Chiropractic Couloir
text: [overview] A curving snow couloir that stands out in spring and can be seen from the town below.
[overview] A huge cornice at the top holds into early May, and snow has mostly melted by early June.
[overview] Moving fast on a cold morning and leaving left near the upper end avoids the cornice.
[overview] Should the cornice release partway up and take a climber off their feet, a cliff of 50 feet below is the risk.
[detailed_rack] Pickets, a few rock pieces, or both can protect it.
[approach] From the Glacier Gorge side, follow the route toward Andrews Glacier and turn left into The Gash, the hanging valley between the glacier and Sharkstooth.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.
[descent_text] The couloir ends on the ridge above a broad, fan-shaped headwall, and a large cornice often guards the top into spring.
[descent_text] Exiting left avoids the cornice.
[descent_text] From the crest, turn north (right) to Andrews Glacier and descend it to the Andrews Glacier trail.
[descent_text] The glacier is a snow slope that firms up to ice late in the year, so carry an axe and crampons.

name: Queen's Way
text: [overview] A route up Apache by way of the Isabelle Glacier, entering from the head of the South Saint Vrain valley.

[approach] From the Brainard Lake area start at the Long Lake trailhead and follow the Pawnee Pass trail past Long Lake to Lake Isabelle, then continue west along the Isabelle Glacier trail to the tarn below Navajo, Apache and Shoshoni peaks.
[approach] Cross the Isabelle Glacier to its southwest corner, where the route climbs a steep snow ramp to a saddle below the summit.
[approach] These are steep snow slopes in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast first.

name: Ariana
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.
[descent_text] Four more rappels end on the snowfield;

name: Astromarmot
text: [overview] The start sits near the snowfield's upper right corner, around 12,600 ft.

name: Birds of Fire
text: [overview] From the snowfield you reach a giant flake, go out right past bolts, cross a roof on cams and continue by a few more bolts toward a pin on a ledge.

name: Black Dagger
text: [approach] Scramble around the north side of the lake beneath the east face and aim for North Chimney, the hidden gully below the middle of the Diamond with a snow tongue reaching into it;
[approach] North Chimney is loose fourth and low fifth class (about 5.4) with snow early in the season, so keep out from under other parties and expect rockfall.
[descent_text] Rappel to Broadway, then cross Broadway to the right to the second rappel line beneath the Casual Route and make four rappels down to the snowfield, the last three on two ropes.

name: Miller's Face

name: Block Party
text: [approach] Work up a big snow patch that slants right, then traverse right to a massive boulder, about level with the foot of the climb;

name: Central Buttress
text: [overview] Descent, fastest: 20 minutes north on the Continental Divide, then Andrews Glacier and Andrews Creek.
[overview] Alternatively walk ten minutes to the North Gully, downclimb its first 100' (steep snow), then descend 800' by plunge-stepping to the base snowfield.

name: South Face
text: [overview] Depending on the year, possibly the gentlest, most secure line up the peak: tidy scrambling plus moderate snow in place of the northwest gully's ice and rubble.

name: East Face/Dallas Peak
text: [overview] A snowy couloir reaches the crest;

name: Forgotten Arete
text: [overview] Approach: follow the trail through Glacier Gorge toward Green Lake, ascend the North Gully, which lies between Pagoda Mountain and the Keyboard of the Winds, to the foot of Sievers' Tower, then go east along the foot of the Keyboards to Jackpot Tower.

name: Forgotten North Face
text: [overview] Approach: Glacier Gorge toward Green Lake, up the North Gully between Pagoda Mountain and the Keyboard of the Winds to the foot of Sievers' Tower, then east along the foot of the Keyboards to Mrs.

name: Glacier Gorge Traverse
text: [overview] A ridge traverse around the cirque of Glacier Gorge, from Arrowhead to Longs, with exposed scrambling and climbing.

name: First Star Couloir
text: [detailed_rack] Optional protection: flukes and pickets.
[approach] Mary's Glacier trailhead walk the steep road to St.
[approach] Mary's Lake, go around its north side, and climb the glacier to the plain of Jamaica Flats.
